## Summary

- Removed redundant `async`/`await` wrappers and `Promise.resolve()` calls around `.dispose()` operations inside `.map()` loops.
- Replaced constructs like `handles.map(async (handle) => { await handle.dispose(); })` and `handles.map((handle) => Promise.resolve(handle.dispose()))` with the cleaner `handles.map((handle) => handle.dispose())`.
- Applied this cleanup globally across `src/models`, `src/presets`, and `src/runtime`.

## Why this change

Passing an `async` callback to `Array.prototype.map()` creates a new Promise for every element, even if the underlying operation (`dispose()`) is straightforward. Additionally, wrapping `handle.dispose()` in `Promise.resolve()` is redundant because `Promise.all()` handles both Promises and synchronous values correctly. Removing these intermediate wrappers reduces micro-allocations in hot resource cleanup paths, slightly improving efficiency and significantly improving code readability.

## Implementation notes

Used targeted replacement to ensure consistent formatting across all model families (e.g., NEMO, Qwen, SenseVoice, Whisper, Wav2Vec2) and runtime components where `Promise.all` is used for bulk disposal.

## Verification

Commands run:
- `npm run build`: Success
- `npm run lint`: Success
- `npm run test`: All 1849 tests passed.

## Risk

Very low risk. If a `.dispose()` method returns a Promise, `Promise.all()` will correctly await it just as it did before. If `.dispose()` is synchronous, `Promise.all()` will resolve it immediately, which is completely safe. The lexical `this` context is preserved since the method is called directly on the object reference.

## Performance impact

Minor reduction in memory allocations during model/session disposal by skipping unnecessary intermediate Promise creation.
